column1: # Firmware that is NOT bundled but worth watching, and why (scripts/check-firmware-updates.py). Columns: name, kind (github | page), target, seen, why.
# "seen" is the release tag (github) or the digest of the page's licence-bearing lines (page) the maintainer last read; --write-seen updates it after a review.
# Bundled firmware is not listed here: it is checked from the manifests.

column5: Closed: "copyright 2026 Xfer Inc. All rights reserved", free beta, no source and no redistribution grant (2026-11-16). Ask steve@xferrecords.com for permission to redistribute, or watch for an open licence.
GPL-3.0 but its source carries a reserved icon atlas (terms unpublished): bundle once it drops it.
GPL-3.0 but embeds Casio CZ-1 and Sequential Prophet-5/10 factory data: bundle once that is dropped or licensed.
GPL-3.0 with TR-909 hat/ride/crash samples via a third-party project and a break generator used by permission: maintainer's call.
MIT repository, GPL-3.0-only firmware: would fit the copyleft pack.

GPL-3.0-only code, but its LICENSING.md lists third-party data outside the allowlist: the Hanan Cumbia sounds and patterns (CC BY-SA 3.0, not GPL-3.0 compatible if counted as one work), three songs from openly licensed editions (CC BY-SA 3.0, CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0), a Johnny Canales portrait and photograph the author says are cleared, and TR-727 recordings the author says are theirs. Read 2026-11-17 (release compas-v1.2-editor.1, hashes match its SHA256SUMS; the release ships its own source). The maintainer chose to leave it out until the data is shown to be separable or the allowlist is widened on purpose. It is the one firmware predicted to keep up on an R36S (docs/R36S-FIRMWARE.md).
